prerequisites: Basic notions of Differential and Integral Calculus
Basic notions of Mechanics and Thermodynamics
Basic notions of Waves and Electromagnetism

learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with basic knowledge about the utility of automatic control systems and their applications in industry and consumer products.
Enable students to mathematically describe and analyze the behavior of a system in the time and frequency domains, using simulation tools.
Enable students to tune controllers in simple control structures.
Know and identify the elements involved in instrumentation for industrial process control and automation and their functions.
Configure and program simple applications in industrial control devices.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. Introduction to process automation and control.
Topic 2. Automation: Introduction to automation. Elements of automation. Regulations. Grafcet diagrams. Programming using SFC and ST.
Topic 3. System modeling: Systems and signals. Functional diagrams. Transfer function. Block diagrams. State-space modeling. System linearization.
Topic 4. System analysis: Stability. Overdamped and underdamped proper modes. Temporal response.

Topic 5. System control: Introduction to control. Steady-state analysis in feedback systems. Transient analysis of feedback systems. Root locus. PID design in the time domain. Digital implementation of controllers.
Topic 6. Frequency domain: Concept of frequency response. Bode and polar diagrams. Time-frequency relationships. Frequency analysis of feedback systems. Controller design in frequency.
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, a minimum score of 4 out of 10 points is required for the theoretical block. If this minimum is met, the final grade is calculated as (0.2 × T1) + (0.6 × T2) + (0.2 × P); otherwise, the grade is the minimum of this formula and 4.0. For the extraordinary call, a theoretical exam (TEX) and practical exam are given; a minimum of 4 out of 10 points is required in the theoretical part. If the theoretical minimum is met, the final grade is (0.8 × TEX) + (0.2 × P); otherwise, the grade is the minimum of this formula and 4.0. Laboratory practice grades are retained until the January call of the following academic year.
